claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a well-characterized hierarchical heterostructure.
High-resolution imaging and phase-characterization data can provide quantitative descriptors of the HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure.
A regression model using microstructural heterogeneity descriptors will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior more accurately than conventional finite-element simulations.
The regression model will generate predictions more rapidly than conventional finite-element simulations.
The spatial distribution of grain boundaries mediates local stress distribution and failure mechanisms.
Dendritic-region statistics are relevant to mechanical strength and fracture behavior.
Phase distributions and phase complexity influence mechanical response.
Linking quantitative heterogeneity features to mechanical responses can improve prediction of alloy properties.
The proposed model will account for local stress concentrations.
The proposed model will account for phase-specific deformation.
Established finite-element simulations for this comparison rely on homogenized material-property assumptions.
Predictive accuracy for Young's modulus and yield strength will improve by approximately 15% relative to finite-element methods.
Computational time will decrease by approximately 50% relative to finite-element methods.
The model will predict fracture behavior more reliably across different stress regimes.
Insufficient imaging resolution of heterostructural features may cause the model to fail.
Extreme local heterogeneity or nonlinear deformation mechanisms absent from the training data may cause the model to fail.
Mechanical responses vary with loading temperature and strain conditions.
The magnitude of predictive gains may vary with microstructural-data quality and loading conditions.
The estimated 15% accuracy gain and 50% time reduction are based on analogous high-entropy-alloy studies.

Failure to attain both the stated accuracy improvement and computational-time reduction, or statistically unacceptable disagreement with independent measurements, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
